title: The Ocean Dragon
prompt:
Character bible:
Children (draw these the same way on every page):
- Elliott, age 4–5, short straight light-brown hair; big gray-blue eyes; round cheeks; friendly adventurous expression, wearing medieval tunic with belt and boots or casual explorer outfit
- Colette, age 2–3, wavy brown hair in a top knot; large gray-blue eyes; soft cheeks, wearing whimsical princess-meets-adventurer dress with floral or heart motifs
Pets (draw these the same way on every page):
- Winnie, a Chihuahua–Pug mix, tan fur; upright ears; curled tail; small size
Keep these characters consistent. They represent specific real children. Do NOT replace them with generic children or idealized animated characters. Preserve their recognizable facial structure.

clean black ink line drawing suitable for coloring
Clean black outlines on white.
No shading, no gray, no gradients, no shadows.
Avoid large filled-black regions; keep interiors open for coloring.

Avoid exaggerated cartoon faces or oversized eyes.
Preserve the real facial proportions from the reference images.

FULL-PAGE COMPOSITION: dynamic vertical composition.
Elliott & Colette and Winnie
fill most of the lower two-thirds.
Key elements extend upward toward the top edge.



SCENE:
On a wide sandy shore,
Elliott & Colette stand beside rolling waves.

A graceful ocean dragon rises from the water,
its body long and flowing like the sea.

Winnie stands at the shoreline.

GLOBAL SAFETY (IMPORTANT):
- No object intersections or impossible overlaps.
- Clean occlusion: if objects overlap, the front object clearly covers the back object.
- No extra limbs, no duplicated faces, no merged hands/feet.
- Keep dragons anatomically clean: one head, two wings (if winged), four limbs, one tail.
- Keep shapes simple and readable for coloring.

Use the attached character sheet reference images as the canonical identity and style.
